title: Numbers and shapes
subtitle: four fifths, seven cubed, rectangular, spherical
summary: Learn how to say fractions, decimals, percentages and long numbers aloud, and the names and adjectives for the commonest two- and three-dimensional shapes.

lesson.heading: Saying numbers aloud
rows: eight to the power of four

lesson.heading: Decimals, commas and long numbers
lesson.text: In English, decimal fractions are separated by a dot, not a comma, and the dot is said as **point**. Commas separate each set of three digits in long numbers, and each set is said separately.

examples.text: 1,623,457 = one **million**, six hundred and twenty-three **thousand**, four hundred and fifty-seven
Telephone numbers: 01223 20675 = oh one **double** two three, two oh six, seven five.

lesson.note: When saying a long number, each group of up to three digits has rising intonation, and the intonation falls on the last group to show the number is complete.

lesson.heading: Two-dimensional shapes
rows: shaped a bit like an egg
four sides of equal length and four right angles
four sides and four right angles, but longer than it is wide

lesson.heading: Parts of a circle
lesson.text: A circle is cut in half by its **diameter**, and the two halves are called **semi-circles**. The **radius** is the distance from the centre of a circle to the **circumference**, the line that goes all the way round it.

examples.text: A **rectangle** has four right angles, and a **pentagon** has five sides.
The **radius** of this circle is 5cm, so its **diameter** is 10cm.
Cut the pizza along the **diameter** and you get two **semi-circles**.

lesson.heading: Three-dimensional shapes
rows: a three-dimensional round shape, like a ball
a three-dimensional square shape, like a dice
a shape with a square base and four triangular sides meeting at a point
a shape that curves round and round a central point, like a spring
lesson.note: The two halves of a sphere are called hemispheres.

lesson.heading: Arithmetic
rows: six times seven is forty-two, or six sevens are forty-two
three z divided by four x, or three z over four x
lesson.note: 6 x 7 = 42 has three natural spoken forms: six times seven is forty-two, six multiplied by seven is forty-two, or six sevens are forty-two.

lesson.text: Watch the -s: it is *seven nines are sixty-three* and *eleven sixteenths*, not ~~seven nine~~ or ~~eleven sixteens~~.

exercises.prompt: Match each shape with its adjective.
Match each description with the name of the shape.

pairs.left: shaped a bit like an egg
four sides of equal length and four right angles

exercises.prompt: Name two shapes that have four right angles: a square and a ___.
exercises.explanation: A rectangle has four right angles, like a square, but its sides are not all equal.

exercises.prompt: 17.1% is said as seventeen ___ one per cent.
exercises.explanation: In English the decimal separator is a dot and it is said as point.
The form is squared: three squared, seven cubed, eight to the power of four.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 6 to the power of 9?
options: six to the power of nine
six at the power of nine
exercises.explanation: The fixed phrase is to the power of.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 11/16 of the students passed the exam?
options: eleven over sixteens of the students
exercises.explanation: Fractions use the ordinal with -s in the plural: four fifths, eleven sixteenths.

exercises.prompt: How do you say the dimensions 3m x 6m?
exercises.explanation: Dimensions use by: ten metres by twelve metres.

exercises.statement: 7 x 9 = 63 can be said as 'Seven nines are sixty-three.'
exercises.explanation: Correct - six sevens are forty-two, seven nines are sixty-three. Note the plural -s.

exercises.statement: 18 C is said as 'eighteen points Celsius'.
exercises.explanation: It is said as eighteen degrees Celsius.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to say 8,556,981 in words.
exercises.answer: eight million, five hundred and fifty-six thousand, nine hundred and eighty-one
exercises.explanation: Each set of three digits is said separately, with and before the final tens and units.

exercises.prompt: Is each shape two-dimensional or three-dimensional?
The distance from the centre of a circle to its circumference is called the ___.
exercises.explanation: The radius runs from the centre to the circumference; the diameter runs right across the circle.
